capture.final_message:
Use extensionality and linear-order case splits.

- For the first conjunct, prove injectivity of \(a \mapsto (a,\infty)\): equality of the rays gives both \(a \le b\) and \(b \le a\). For instance, \(a<b\) would put \(b\) in \(Ioi(a)\) but not in \(Ioi(b)\). Antisymmetry then yields \(a=b\); the converse is immediate.

- For the second, apply set extensionality and reduce membership to
  \[
  (a<x\land x<b)\ \lor\ c<x \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \min(a,c)<x.
  \]
  Split on \(a<b\). If \(b\le a\), the hypothesis \(c<\max(a,b)=a\) makes the open interval empty and \(\min(a,c)=c\). If \(a<b\), split further on \(c\le a\) versus \(a<c\); in the latter case the hypothesis gives \(c<b\), so \((a,b)\) fills exactly the portion of \(Ioi(a)\) not already covered by \(Ioi(c)\). Linear-order reasoning then proves the pointwise equivalence.
